The classical Boussinesq system revisitedThanks:  1Institut Denis Poisson, Université de Tours, Université d’Orléans, CNRS, Parc Grandmont, 37200, France (luc.molinet@univ-tours.fr).Thanks:  2Laboratoire de mathématiques-EDST, Faculté des Sciences et EDST, Université Libanaise, Hadat, Liban (rtalhouk@ul.edu.lb), (zibtissame@hotmail.com)

Luc Molinet1 , Raafat Talhouk2 and Ibtissam Zaiter2
Abstract.

In this work, we revisit the study by M. E. Schonbek [11] concerning the problem of existence of global entropic weak solutions for the classical Boussinesq system, as well as the study of the regularity of these solutions by C. J. Amick [1]. We propose to regularize by a ”fractal” operator (i.e. a differential operator defined by a Fourier multiplier of type ϵ|ξ|λ,(ϵ,λ)∈ℝ+×]0,2]\epsilon|\xi|^{\lambda},\,(\epsilon,\lambda)\in\,\mathbb{R}_{+}\times]0,2]). We first show that the regularized system is globally unconditionally well-posed in Sobolev spaces of type Hs​(ℝ),s>12,H^{s}(\mathbb{R}),\,s>\frac{1}{2}, uniformly in the regularizing parameters (ϵ,λ)∈ℝ+×]0,2](\epsilon,\lambda)\in\,\mathbb{R}_{+}\times]0,2]. As a consequence we obtain the global well-posedness of the classical Boussinesq system at this level of regularity as well as the convergence in the strong topology of the solution of the regularized system towards the solution of the classical Boussinesq equation as the parameter ϵ\epsilon goes to 00. In a second time, we prove the existence of low regularity entropic solutions of the Boussinesq equations emanating from u0∈H1u_{0}\in H^{1} and ζ0\zeta_{0} in an Orlicz class as weak limits of regular solutions.

Key words and phrases: 
Boussinesq system, global existence, entropy solution, fractal regularization.
2010 Mathematics Subject Classification
35Q35,35L56,35B30

1. Introduction

In this paper we are concerned with the classical Boussinesq system, introduced by J. V. Boussinesq in 1871 to describe weak amplitude long wave propagation on the surface of ideal incompressible liquid for irrotational flow submitted to gravitational force where the surface tension has been neglected. In 2002, Bona, Chen and Saut [3] have derived a class of models called four parameters Boussinesq systems. The corresponding PDE’s system is given by:

{ζt+ux+(u​ζ)x+a​ux​x​x−b​ζx​x​t=0,ut+ζx+u​ux+c​ζx​x​x−d​ux​x​t=0.\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{lcl}\zeta_{t}+u_{x}+(u\zeta)_{x}+au_{xxx}-b\zeta_{xxt}&=&0,\\ u_{t}+\zeta_{x}+uu_{x}+c\zeta_{xxx}-du_{xxt}&=&0.\end{array}\right.

ζ⁡(x,t)+1\zeta(x,t)+1 corrrespond to the normalized total height of the liquid and then describe the free surface of the liquid, xx is the spatial position which is proportional to distance in the direction of propagation. u⁡(x,t)u(x,t) is the horizontal velocity field of the liquid particle which is at position xx at time t.t. a,b,ca,b,c and dd are four parameters verifying consistence relation (see [3]). The classical Boussinesq system corresponds to the choice of parameters: a=b=c=0a=b=c=0 and d=1d=1 and the system becomes:

{ζt+ux+(u​ζ)x=0,ut+ζx+u​ux−ux​x​t=0.\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{lcl}\zeta_{t}+u_{x}+(u\zeta)_{x}&=&0,\\ u_{t}+\zeta_{x}+uu_{x}-u_{xxt}&=&0.\end{array}\right.

Schonbek (in [11]) have shown the existence of global in time weak solution under a natural non-cavitation condition (1+ζ0>01+\zeta_{0}>0) with initial data ζ0\zeta_{0} in some Orlicz class and u0∈H1​(ℝ).u_{0}\in H^{1}(\mathbb{R}). She used a viscosity method by regularizing the first equation with the Laplace operator after what a uniform entropic estimate is established. This entropic estimate allowed to passing to the limit and defining a weak solution for the classical Boussinesq system. Amick (in [1]) showed that weak solutions given by Schonbek are in fact infinitely regular, i.e. in C0∞C_{0}^{\infty} if the initial data are Cc∞.C^{\infty}_{c}. Actually the results of Amick are implicitly containing also that the entropic solution is in HkH^{k} if the initial data are in classical regular spaces of type ℍ𝕜×ℍ𝕜+𝟙,∀𝕜∈ℕ,𝕜≥𝟚.\mathbb{H^{k}\times H^{k+1},\forall k\in\mathbb{N},\,k\geq 2}. Bona & all. (in [4]) studied many cases of giving a,b,c,da,\,b,\,c,\,d parameters and in particular concerning system (1) they give, without proof, existence and uniqueness results of solution (ζ,u)∈C⁡([0,T],Hs×Hs+1)(\zeta,u)\in C([0,T];H^{s}\times H^{s+1}) for given initial data in Hs×Hs+1,s≥1H^{s}\times H^{s+1},\;s\geq 1 with infx∈ℝ(1+ζ0​(x))>0\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}}(1+\zeta_{0}(x))>0 and announcing the continuity of the flow on more restricted class of initial data. All the previous studies are in one dimension, many other studies of the four parameters Boussinesq system in the last ten years concerning the two dimensional case, see for instance [10] and references therein.

In our work we reconsider the method of regularization by using generalized derivative operator, also called ”fractal” operator, that is a differential operator defined by a Fourier multiplier of type |ξ|λ,λ∈]0,2].|\xi|^{\lambda},\,\lambda\in]0,2]. More precisely we consider the following regularized system:

{ζt+ux+(u​ζ)x+ϵ​gλ​(ζ)=0,ut+ζx+u​ux−ux​x​t=0.\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{lcl}\zeta_{t}+u_{x}+(u\zeta)_{x}+\epsilon g_{\lambda}(\zeta)&=&0,\\ u_{t}+\zeta_{x}+uu_{x}-u_{xxt}&=&0.\end{array}\right.

where gg is the non-local operator defined through the Fourier transform by

ℱ(g[φ(t,⋅)])(ξ)=|ξ|λℱ(φ(t,⋅))(ξ), with λ∈]0,2].\mathcal{F}(g[\varphi(t,\cdot)])(\xi)=|\xi|^{\lambda}\mathcal{F}(\varphi(t,\cdot))(\xi),\;\;\mbox{ with }\lambda\in]0,2]. (1.10)

We show that this system is locally in time unconditionally well posed in Hs×Hs+1H^{s}\times H^{s+1} for s>12s>\frac{1}{2} uniformly with respect to the parameter ϵ≥0\epsilon\geq 0 and λ>0\lambda>0. In particular we get the convergence in C⁡([0,T],Hs×Hs+1)C([0,T];H^{s}\times H^{s+1}) of the solutions to (1) towards the solutions to the Boussinesq equation (1) as the parameter ϵ\epsilon tends to 00. Then we prove that the analysis of Schonbek to establish the entropic estimate still work for (1) so that we can extend our solutions for all positive times. Finally we prove that the low regularity entropic solutions of the Boussinesq equation with u0∈H1u_{0}\in H^{1} and ξ\xi in an Orlicz class can also be obtained as limits of regular solutions by regularizing the initial datas and using our main convergence results. We prove also the continuity of the flow map. All the previous results are obtained only under the non zero-depth condition 1+ζ0>0.1+\zeta_{0}>0.

(1.11)

Definition 1.2.

Let s>1/2s>1/2. We will say that the Cauchy problem associated with (1) is unconditionally globally well-posed in Hs​(ℝ)×Hs+1​(ℝ)H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s+1}(\mathbb{R}) if for any initial data (ζ0,u0)∈Hs​(ℝ)×Hs+1​(ℝ)(\zeta_{0},u_{0})\in H^{s}({\mathbb{R}})\times H^{s+1}(\mathbb{R}) there exists a solution (ζ,u)∈C⁡(ℝ+,Hs​(ℝ)×Hs+1​(ℝ))(\zeta,u)\in C(\mathbb{R}_{+}\,;H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s+1}(\mathbb{R})) to (1) emanating from (ζ0,u0)(\zeta_{0},u_{0}). For any ϵ≥0\epsilon\geq 0, λ∈]0,2]\lambda\in]0,2] and any s>1/2s>1/2, the Cauchy problem (1) is unconditionally globally well-posed in Hs​(ℝ)×Hs+1​(ℝ)H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s+1}(\mathbb{R}).

(ζϵ,λ,uϵ,λ)​⟶ϵ→0​(ζ,u)​ in ​C​([0,T],Hs​(ℝ)×Hs+1​(ℝ)).(\zeta^{\epsilon,\lambda},u^{\epsilon,\lambda})\begin{array}[t]{c}\longrightarrow\\ {\scriptstyle\epsilon\to 0}\end{array}(\zeta,u)\text{ in }C([0,T],H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s+1}(\mathbb{R}))\;. (1.12)

3. Local existence for the regularized system and energy estimates

3.1. Local well-posedness and estimates for a Bona-Smith’s approximation

We fix ϵ>0\epsilon>0 in (1). For μ>0\mu>0 we consider the Bona-Smith’s type regularization problem associated to (1)

{ζt−μ​ζt​x​x+ux+(u​ζ)x+ϵ​gλ​(ζ)=0,ut−ux​x​t+ζx+u​ux=0,(ζ,u)​(0)=(ζ0,u0).\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{lcl}\zeta_{t}-\mu\zeta_{txx}+u_{x}+(u\zeta)_{x}+\epsilon g_{\lambda}(\zeta)&=&0,\\ u_{t}-u_{xxt}+\zeta_{x}+uu_{x}&=&0,\\ (\zeta,u)(0)&=(\zeta_{0},u_{0}).&\end{array}\right.

Setting V=(ζ,u)V=(\zeta,u), (3.1) can be rewritten as

dd​t​V=Ωμ​(V)\frac{d}{dt}V=\Omega_{\mu}(V) (3.24)

where

Ωμ(V)=((1−μ∂x2)−1[−ux−(uζ)x−ϵgλ(ζ)],(1−∂x2)−1[−ζx−uux])\Omega_{\mu}(V)=\Bigl((1-\mu\partial_{x}^{2})^{-1}[-u_{x}-(u\zeta)_{x}-\epsilon g_{\lambda}(\zeta)],\;(1-\partial_{x}^{2})^{-1}[-\zeta_{x}-uu_{x}]\Bigr)

In this section, we establish the global existence for any fixed ϵ≥0\epsilon\geq 0 of (1). This completes the proof of Theorem 1.1. To obtain the uniform estimates, we proceed as in [11] by constructing a convex positive entropy for the associated hyperbolic system

{ζt+(u+u​ζ)x=0,ut+(ζ+u22)x=0.\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{lcl}\zeta_{t}+(u+u\zeta)_{x}&=&0,\\ u_{t}+(\zeta+\frac{u^{2}}{2})_{x}&=&0.\end{array}\right.

Finally we can state the following theorem as a consequence of the previous results.

Theorem 4.1.

Let s>1/2s>1/2. For (ζ0,u0)∈Hs×Hs+1(\zeta_{0},u_{0})\in H^{s}\times H^{s+1} such that 1+ζ0>01+\zeta_{0}>0, the classical Boussinesq system (1) has a unique solution (ζ,u)(\zeta,u) in C⁡(ℝ+,Hs×Hs+1)∩C1​(ℝ+,Hs−1×Hs)C(\mathbb{R}^{+},H^{s}\times H^{s+1})\cap C^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{+},H^{s-1}\times H^{s}).
The flot-map S:(ζ0,u0)⟶(ζ,u)S:(\zeta_{0},u_{0})\longrightarrow(\zeta,u) is continuous from Hs×Hs+1H^{s}\times H^{s+1} into C⁡(ℝ+,Hs​(ℝ)×Hs+1​(ℝ))C(\mathbb{R}^{+};H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s+1}(\mathbb{R})).

5. Global entropy solutions of the Boussinesq system

In this section, we study existence of weak solution for the Boussinesq system (1) for initial condition (ζ0,u0)∈Λσ0×H1(\zeta_{0},u_{0})\in\Lambda_{\sigma_{0}}\times H^{1}. To do so, we regularize the initial data by a mollifiers sequence (ρn)n⊂D⁡(ℝ)(\rho_{n})_{n}\subset D(\mathbb{R}) by setting ζ0,n=ρn∗ζ0\zeta_{0,n}=\rho_{n}*\zeta_{0} and u0,n=ρn∗u0u_{0,n}=\rho_{n}*u_{0}, where ρn(⋅)=nρ(n⋅),ρ∈D(ℝ)\rho_{n}(\cdot)=n\rho(n\cdot),\;\rho\in D(\mathbb{R}) such that

0≤ρ≤1, supp ​ρ⊂[0,1]​ and ​∫ℝρ​𝑑x=1.0\leq\rho\leq 1,\mbox{ supp }\rho\subset[0,1]\mbox{ and }\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}}\rho dx=1.

Note that (u0,n)n⊂Hs(u_{0,n})_{n}\subset H^{s} and it is bounded in H1H^{1} with ‖u0,n‖H1≤‖u0‖H1\|u_{0,n}\|_{H^{1}}\leq\|u_{0}\|_{H^{1}} and u0,n→u0u_{0,n}\to u_{0} in H1​(ℝ)H^{1}(\mathbb{R}). For ζ0,n\zeta_{0,n}, we first notice that ζ0∈Λσ0\zeta_{0}\in\Lambda_{\sigma_{0}} ensures that 1+ζ0>01+\zeta_{0}>0 a.e. on ℝ\mathbb{R}. Since 1+ζ0,n=ρn∗(1+ζ0)1+\zeta_{0,n}=\rho_{n}*(1+\zeta_{0}), it follows that 1+ζ0,n>01+\zeta_{0,n}>0 on ℝ\mathbb{R}. Moreover, using (4.73) and proceeding exactly as (4) by replacing e−|⋅|e^{-|\cdot|} by ρn\rho_{n} it is straightforward to check that ζ0,n∈L2\zeta_{0,n}\in L^{2} with |ζ0,n|L2≤cn​|ζ0|Λσ0|\zeta_{0,n}|_{L^{2}}\leq c_{n}|\zeta_{0}|_{\Lambda_{\sigma_{0}}} where cnc_{n} depends on ‖ρn‖L2\|\rho_{n}\|_{L^{2}}. Similary, we can verify that ζ0,n∈Hs\zeta_{0,n}\in H^{s}, for s≥0s\geq 0.
Now, consider (ζn,un)(\zeta_{n},u_{n}) the solution of (1) emanating from (ζ0,n,u0,n)(\zeta_{0,n},u_{0,n}) given by Proposition 4.2. we will prove that (ζn,un)(\zeta_{n},u_{n}) has a subsequence which converges to a weak solution of the Boussinesq system (1) with initial data (ζ0,u0)(\zeta_{0},u_{0}). Note that (ζn,un)(\zeta_{n},u_{n}) satisfies the entropy estimate (4.74) which implies

‖un​(t)‖H12+∫−∞+∞σ0​(1+ζn)​𝑑x≤‖u0,n‖H12+∫−∞+∞σ0​(1+ζ0,n)​𝑑x.\|u_{n}(t)\|_{H^{1}}^{2}+\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\sigma_{0}(1+\zeta_{n})dx\leq\|u_{0,n}\|_{H^{1}}^{2}+\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\sigma_{0}(1+\zeta_{0,n})dx\;.

The H1H^{1}-convergence of (u0,n)(u_{0,n}) towards u0u_{0} ensures that the first term of the above right-hand side converges to ‖u0‖H12\|u_{0}\|_{H^{1}}^{2}. For the second term one has to work a little more. We follow [11] and use the convexity of σ0\sigma_{0} and Jensen inequality to get that

σ0(1+ζ0,n)=σ0(∫ℝ(1+ζ0)ρn(⋅−z)dz)≤∫ℝσ0(1+ζ0)ρn(⋅−z)dz.\sigma_{0}(1+\zeta_{0,n})=\sigma_{0}\Bigl(\int_{\mathbb{R}}(1+\zeta_{0})\rho_{n}(\cdot-z)dz\Bigr)\leq\int_{\mathbb{R}}\sigma_{0}(1+\zeta_{0})\rho_{n}(\cdot-z)dz\;.

Therefore, integrating on ℝ\mathbb{R}, using Fubini and ∫ℝρn=1\int_{\mathbb{R}}\rho_{n}=1, we obtain

∫−∞+∞σ0​(1+ζ0,n)​𝑑x≤∫−∞+∞σ0​(1+ζ0)​𝑑x.\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\sigma_{0}(1+\zeta_{0,n})dx\leq\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\sigma_{0}(1+\zeta_{0})dx\;.

We thus are lead to the following uniform estimate on ℝ+\mathbb{R}_{+} :

‖un​(t)‖H12+∫−∞+∞σ0​(1+ζn​(t))​𝑑x≤‖u0‖H12+∫−∞+∞σ0​(1+ζ0)​𝑑x.\|u_{n}(t)\|_{H^{1}}^{2}+\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\sigma_{0}(1+\zeta_{n}(t))dx\leq\|u_{0}\|_{H^{1}}^{2}+\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\sigma_{0}(1+\zeta_{0})dx\;. (5.113)

In the sequel we will make a constant use of the following lemma that can be easily deduced from (4.73) and (5.113).

Lemma 5.1.

let χ∈L1​(ℝ)∩L∞​(ℝ)\chi\in L^{1}(\mathbb{R})\cap L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}). Then

∫ℝ|ζn​(t,x)​χ​(x)|​𝑑x≤c,\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}}\left|\zeta_{n}(t,x)\chi(x)\right|dx\leq c, (5.114)

for all tt, where cc is independent of nn.

∫ℝ|ζn​(t,x)|​|χ⁡(x)|​𝑑x=∫{x/−1<ζn(t,x)|≤M}|ζn(t,x)||χ(x)|dx+∫{x/ζn(t,x)≥M}|ζn(t,x)χ(x)|dx≤M​∫ℝ|χ⁡(x)|​dx+|χ|L∞​∫ℝσ0​(1+ζn​(t,x))​dx≤c.\displaystyle\begin{array}[]{lcl}\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\zeta_{n}(t,x)||\chi(x)|dx&=&\displaystyle\int_{\{x/{-1<\zeta_{n}(t,x)|\leq M}\}}|\zeta_{n}(t,x)||\chi(x)|dx\\ &&\quad+\displaystyle\int_{\{x/{\zeta_{n}(t,x)\geq M}\}}|\zeta_{n}(t,x)\chi(x)|dx\\ &\leq&M\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\chi(x)|dx+|\chi|_{L^{\infty}}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\sigma_{0}(1+\zeta_{n}(t,x))dx\leq c.\end{array}

∎
